# Creating Dresscode compatible Mods

## By YIIS

![][image1]

This guide will walk you through how to use Alpakit and FF7RML from the custom engine update to create Dresscode compatible mods.  
I will try to keep it beginner friendly and only cover how to create data mods for character outfits and weapons for use in Dresscode since that will benefit the overwhelming majority of mods in this game. I will not cover how to create the actual edits (as in new models, textures etc), for that check a different guide first.

A more technical documentation about how to use the modloader to create actual blueprint systems like Dresscode will be posted at a later date, just ask in the [OpenFF7R](https://discord.gg/FTP8WZY2) Discord and I’ll probably respond at some point with a quick rundown.

# Prerequisites

Custom Unreal Engine build: [https://github.com/narknon/UnrealEngine-CEEnd/tree/7Reb](https://github.com/narknon/UnrealEngine-CEEnd/tree/7Reb)  
Updated Rebirth project files: [https://github.com/narknon/FF7R2UProj](https://github.com/narknon/FF7R2UProj)

If you have troubles setting everything up you can check out this guide: 

[How to set up Narknon's Custom FF7 Rebirth Engine](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1l6wloaJ1cRtLbQsqtlEATghIxv26bnUd2hP59R1U_qg/edit?tab=t.0)

It’s really not great in some aspects, it’s telling you to download 3 different versions of visual studio lol. But I couldn’t find another one quickly, so if you have struggles, do what it says.

**Except**, make sure to download the latest builds (at least v4) from the **Releases** section.

![][image2]

# Overview

The old workflow required modders to replace current assets to use custom ones because there was no way to reference mods dynamically.  
With this new engine version, a new way of packing your mods was implemented that adds your custom assets to the AssetRegistry which allows them to be referenced dynamically by other mods.  
Instead of packing the normal way and adding \_P to your pak names, you will be packing your mods as DLCs which the game registers natively.

# Alpakit  

In order to create mods that are modloader compatible you need to create a mod plugin. For that you open Alpakit by clicking the icon in the toolbar or in the File Menu.

# ![][image3]

It will list all your mod plugins and also engine and normal project plugins if you check the boxes on the right (really no need to show them though).  
If you downloaded the Version 4 project files, you will have 2 entries by default, **FF7RML** and **FF7RModMenu**. They are included because you will need to reference some base objects from the mod library, but you will not have to build those yourself because everyone should be using the official release build from [Nexus](https://www.nexusmods.com/finalfantasy7rebirth/mods/1061) so that we don’t end up having a bunch of different versions floating around causing things to not be compatible anymore.

![][image4]

There are some settings at the top that will improve your iteration speed immensely.  
You can have Alpakit move your mod automatically to your game directory and run the game after packaging.  
The **FF7RGamePath** should point to the root directory of your game.  
In **Launch Game After Packing** you can specify the platform where you bought the game from to run it automatically.

Click on **Create Mod** to create your first mod plugin, this window should pop up:

![][image5]

Click on **Blueprint Only** and type in a name for your mod to enable the **Create Mod** button.  
After you created it, it will now show up in the list and you can click on **Edit** to open up the properties of your .uplugin file that was created.

![][image6]  
There is unfortunately no simple way to use this data from inside the game, so right now it doesn’t really do anything.  
You probably still want to fill it out so that your mod is compatible in the future if someone creates an external mod manager or something like that.

We will now be working from our mod plugin directory and not from the game content folder.  
If creating a plugin does not reveal a list of plugins in your content browser, you will have to enable that manually.

![][image7]

# 

# FF7RML

FF7RML is the actual mod loader and mod library.  
It provides a collection of objects and extensions that mod creators can inherit from which the modloader scans for at every startup.  
You can create custom extensions that provide their own custom data that people can derive from, you can create actors that just utilizes the assets that the mod loader scans for, or you can just create data mods that systems like Dresscode can use.

If you press the Left and Right stick (or F1 and F2) at the same time, you can open up the Mod Menu that lists your currently installed mods and lets you set some configs if the mods have any.

![][image8]

It will only show ModActors and ModObjects (Blueprints) by default, if you hit triangle it will also include ModData (DataAssets, which we will create in this guide).

## MetaData

In order for your mod to show up correctly in the ModMenu or in Dresscode, you will have to create a MetaData asset that the modloader scans for in every mod plugin.  
It has to be in a specific directory and have a specific name, namely **{your mods content folder}/MetaData/DA\_ModMetaData**.  
So in your content browser, go to your mod plugin directory and create the **MetaData** folder.  
**Right click** in the content browser, go to **Miscellaneous** and create a **DataAsset**.  
Select **PDA\_ModMetaData** as the base and name the asset **DA\_ModMetaData**.

![][image9]

If you open up that file, it will have the same fields as the Property Window from Alpakit.  
This one though **will** be parsed by the ModMenu and Dresscode to display your Mod MetaData in-game.  
So fill this out appropriately. Every time you update your mod, increment your version as well.  
If you are dependent on a mod, usually add them to the Plugins array. FF7RML will always be added as a dependency by default and Dresscode was designed to not create any itself, so you will be fine just leaving this as is.

Import Custom Assets

Dresscode itself is effectively just a runtime **skeletal mesh changer**. It does not create a custom character blueprint or add the costumes to DataObjects. It just changes the mesh reference of your currently active blueprint to a new mesh.  
More sophisticated systems will probably come out in the future since FF7RML is open source and anybody can derive extensions and systems from it.

Most custom outfit or weapon mods create the skeletal mesh at the original location of the asset it is supposed to replace. Additional assets from like materials instances, kdi, bnm, vfx etc can be referenced at any location, but there has to be a root file that needs to be replaced to inject those additional files.  
Usually that’s the skeletal mesh or the character/weapon blueprint.

That’s **not necessary** anymore, you can just put your assets anywhere in your mod plugin directory that you created with Alpakit, the mod loader will look for a DataAsset that we will create in the next step that acts basically as a container for all the custom assets that you want the modloader to have access to.  
So just put everything that is custom in your mod directory and you should be good.  
You can still reference assets from the game, you actually **have** to do that for the **skeleton**.  
Your skeletal mesh still has to reference the skeleton at the original game location because the animation blueprints of the characters have hard refs to that.  
**If you get a T-Pose, this is probably why.**

**TLDR**: So just to make it clear, this is all you need to do:  
\- Create your assets (3d models, textures etc) like you usually do.  
\- Import your custom assets (Skeletal Mesh, Material Instances, KDI, BNM, VFX, etc) anywhere in your mod plugin directory that you created with Alpakit.  
\- Make sure the skeletal mesh has its skeleton at the original game directory. (**probably** only really matters for characters and not weapons)  
\- Reference any game assets (Materials, BNM, etc) as you want.

## ModData Assets

The Modloader scans for several different types of custom assets. The simplest form being DataAssets which only serve to add content (no blueprint logic) to the game.  
Anybody can create a custom asset type and scan for that themselves, but I have provided some basic templates that the ModLoader scans for. This allows systems to not create any additional dependencies and your mods to stay compatible with any new system that any of you create.

If you create a DataAsset anywhere in your mod plugin directory, there are a few basic data types that you can use. 

Just type in **PDA\_ModData** when you pick a class for the DataAsset to get a list of supported data types that you can use to feed assets to the ModLoader.

![][image10]

Dresscode uses **PDA\_ModData\_Character** to look for skeletal meshes. While the rest is scanned and bucketed by the ModLoader, there are currently no systems that use those.  
I might make a quick material/texture replacer that uses some more of these, but the goal with this is that people create their own stuff.  
Anyway, if you want to add a weapon or character skin to Dresscode, just select **PDA\_ModData\_Character.**

The default **ModType** for **Character** is already set, if you want to make a weapon mod change it to **Weapon**.

![][image11]

*(There is an experimental mode for hair in Dresscode, but that method doesn’t really allow me to persist some changes. So I will have the custom hair feature in another mod that does attachment stuff, just letting you know though if you want to tinker).*

You can only have **1 of each** Mod Types as a DataAsset per Mod Plugin.  
So if you have multiple skins that you want to pack as a collection, just add all weapons to one DataAsset with **ModType Weapon**, and all character outfits to another DataAsset with **ModType Character**.  
![][image12]

**General Data** is basically used as menu display info by Dresscode, so give your costume a name and description and select a **Texture2d** or a **Sprite** for the Preview Image.  
**Skeletal Mesh Data** is where you set which **Player Type** your mod is based on, and which **SkeletalMesh** should be used by Dresscode for replacement.  
It will replace your character’s blueprint mesh with this skeletal mesh, you can still give it any AssetUserData (condition mesh, emission, KDB, etc)  that you want etc.  
**Actor** is not used by Dresscode.  
**Additional Data** is supposed to allow you to attach some more custom data or DataObject entries, but it’s not used by Dresscode as well.

# Packing your mod

That's basically it, just open up Alpakit and hit the “alpakit\!” button next to your mod entry in the list. **Don’t** package FF7RML or FFR7ModMenu, always use the release build from Nexus in your game.  
It will only cook and package that specific mod, so if you are like me and you have hundreds of gigs of game assets in your project, this is a blessing.

If you filled out the Alpakit settings, it will move your mod to the correct directory automatically.  
If you didn’t, your mod will be in /*FF7R2UProj/Saved/ArchivedPlugins/* as a zip file.

The mods that you create this way have to be in a different mods folder. So if you don’t already have it, create a folder called **Mods** in *{Game Directory}/End/* so that it is next to you games content folder:

![][image13]![][image14]

# V1.1 Update

A list of extra things that you can use when creating a mod.

## Grouping

Costumes/Weapons can now be grouped. By default, they will be grouped by the *Friendly Name* entry in the MetaData.asset.  
So if you give your mod the same *Friendly Name* in the DA as another mod has, you can effectively now extend that other mod and yours will be grouped with it.

### Custom Grouping

If you have a lot of changes in a single mod plugin but not all are just variants and you want to create extra groups, here’s how you do it manually:  
In your DataAsset where you have your custom entries for weapons and characters, go to an entry, open *Additional Data* and add an entry to *CustomData*.  
Name it **GroupKey**, set the *ConfigType* to string and the the *DefaultString* to a name that will effectively be your group name.  
Do that for every entry that you want to group, all entries that share the same DefaultString will be grouped together.

![][image15]

## Passing Actors

You can now also pass actors instead of just skeletal meshes.  
This allows you to do more sophisticated changes once Dresscode supports them, but for now it allows you to make variations of your costume without having to duplicate the skeletal mesh each time.  
So it will reduce file size if you have a lot of variations.

*This doesn’t work for weapons because weapons don’t use EndMaterialPacks, this will be supported next update though.*

### EndMaterialPack

We will use Square Enix's asset type to pass a collection of materials to the actor.  
Usually you would just right click in your content browser and create the asset type from there.  
But I kinda forgot to add this in the V4 update, so for now just download [this](https://drive.google.com/file/d/15QR_njM9dcLQw5Jz4SLBhM_XGRMMfNB0/view?usp=sharing) dummy and put it in your content browser from outside of unreal.

Fill it out with every material instance that your variation uses.

![][image16]

Give it the **same** name that you have for your material slot in your skeletal mesh.

![][image17]

If you are making a *weapon* mod, create a blueprint of type **EndWeaponSkeletalMeshActor**.  
If you are making a *character* mod  create a blueprint of type **EndPlayerCharacter**.

![][image18]![][image19]

For both, you can just give it a skeletal mesh for your **main** costume/weapon.

![][image20]

This you can pass in the DataAsset in Actor **instead** of using the skeletal mesh field.

If you want to create **variations**, *right click* on the blueprint you just created and create a **child** from it.  
In this one, you only change the MaterialPack to the one with your variations.

![][image21]

You can add this as a new entry in your DataAsset as usual.

# Issues

## Known Problems

There are some known issues in the current Dresscode build.

1. **Field Weapon KDB doesn’t update automatically**: When you select a new weapon, the KDB component still caches data from the previous skeletal mesh. The preview spawns a custom Blueprint where that is no issue and the main menu spawns a new blueprint which will be initialized correctly, but you have to reset the field character manually. I don’t know if there is any quick in-game way to force a reload of the actor, but reloading your save file or restarting the game will definitely do the trick.

2. **Weapon Emission doesn’t update automatically**: Effectively the same issue as 1, except this will additionally not work correctly in the Dresscode preview, it will work correctly in the main menu and after manually resetting the field character as mentioned above. You can do some shenanigans and switch from a weapon that has a blue emissive color to a weapon that has a different color, and it will retain the original emissive color on the new weapon until the actor is resetted.

# Final words

I guess that’s all, if you have questions or find issues, let me know on Discord.  
This guide will be updated over time if issues get fixed or new ones pop up.
